key_insight: Hysteretic Policy Optimization (HPO) stabilizes sparse-reward RL by down-weighting negative-advantage updates and using mean-length normalization, with Adaptive HPO (A-HPO) automatically setting that balance from batch statistics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a simple drop-in change to GRPO-style training that can improve sample efficiency and early-stage learning when rewards are sparse and verifiable.
method: Reduce the update weight for negative-advantage responses instead of treating all advantages symmetrically.
Replace per-response length normalization with mean-length normalization to decouple update magnitude from output length.
Use A-HPO to adapt the hysteretic weight from batch-level advantage-sign statistics, removing manual tuning.
evidence_signal: In TeleLogs and Countdown experiments, A-HPO improved reward per update over GRPO, with the biggest gains in early sparse-reward regimes and a final TeleLogs reward of 0.84.
watch_item: The adaptive hysteretic rule may depend on reliable batch advantage-sign statistics, so behavior could vary with batch size, reward sparsity, and task-specific reward noise.
paper_title: HPO: Hysteretic Policy Optimization for Stable and Efficient Training under Sparse-Reward Regime
